title: The Fall of the Pagans and the Origins of Medieval Christianity
description:
S01 E06 — Jews in the Roman Empire
Knowing what role Judaism plays in the Roman Empire; learning how Rome's experience with this stalwart monotheistic faith, the first it has encountered, differs from the challenge of the Christian faith that emerges from it.

title: The Fall of the Pagans and the Origins of Medieval Christianity
description:
S01 E07 — Christian Challenge - First Conversions
The first years of efforts to convert people to Christianity; the early leadership by James of those who are often called Jewish Christians; the career of Paul, from his own conversion after a vision to his work propagating the message of Jesus.

title: The Fall of the Pagans and the Origins of Medieval Christianity
description:
S01 E08 — Pagan Response - First Persecutions
Early responses to Christianity; the violent persecutions in Rome under Nero; the legalistic and easily avoided persecutions under later emperors; Roman ignorance of Christianity; the eventual momentum that ignorance gives the new faith.

title: Great Ancient Civilizations of Asia Minor
description:
S01 E05 — Origins of Greek Civilization
As the Hittites unite Anatolia, early Greeks called Achaeans visit its western reaches; Achaean warlords trade and raid along the shores of Asia Minor; in time, they become the first Greeks to clash with the armies of a great king to the east.

title: Great Ancient Civilizations of Asia Minor
description:
S01 E06 — The Legend of Troy
The most enduring legacies from early Anatolia are "The Iliad" and "The Odyssey": how the siege of Troy and the exploits of Homer's warrior chieftains fit into the wider tale of imperial struggle and decline during the Greek Dark Age.

title: Great Ancient Civilizations of Asia Minor
description:
S01 E07 — Iron Age Kingdoms of Asia Minor
From 1200 B.C. to 1000 B.C., migrations reshape Anatolia; Phrygians come from the Balkans, only to be overcome by Cimmerian nomads; in the West, Hittite provincials found trade-rich Lydia, whose last king is Croesus.

title: Great Ancient Civilizations of Asia Minor
description:
S01 E08 — Emergence of the Polis
From 750 B.C., the Greeks distinguish themselves with the polis, a city-state based on citizen rule; by 500 B.C., Athens devises the first democratic constitution, with all adult male citizens forming the sovereign assembly.

title: The Architecture of Power: Great Palaces of the Ancient World
description:
S01 E01 — Palaces Past and Present
Exploring the palaces of Saddam Hussein; discovering how he calls upon the ancient Egyptians and Babylonians for inspiration; how the architecture changes over time in response to threats from Iran and the United States.

title: The Architecture of Power: Great Palaces of the Ancient World
description:
S01 E02 — Malkata Palace: Pharaoh, Foreigners, and Gods
Traveling back to the 14th century B.C. in Egypt; how the Malkata Palace represents a microcosm of Egypt; architectural details reveal insights about religious rituals and how pharaohs attempt to assert their domination over others.

title: The Architecture of Power: Great Palaces of the Ancient World
description:
S01 E03 — Amarna: Palace of the First Sun King
Akhenaten shifts Egypt's capital to Amarna; how his worship of the sun disk defines an era built on temple crops, sacrifices and obedience to the pharaoh; how relocating his seat of power helps Akhenaten wrestle authority away from religious leaders.

title: The Architecture of Power: Great Palaces of the Ancient World
description:
S01 E04 — Phaistos: Palaces Between Asia and Europe
Studying Bronze Age Crete; the myth of Daedalus and his labyrinth symbolizes Crete's location at the intersection of multiple cultures; discovering the Phaistos Palace, the site of extravagant religious rituals and entertainment spectacles.

title: The Architecture of Power: Great Palaces of the Ancient World
description:
S01 E05 — Palace of Nestor at Pylos and Bronze Age Greece
Exploring the Palace of Nestor, a complex centered around the throne room; the ancient styles the Mycenaeans develop to bring these elaborate structures to life; what the arrangement of rooms reveals about how royals live and maintain control.

title: Experiencing Rome: A Visual Exploration of Antiquity's Greatest Empire
description:
S01 E01 — Rome-A Spectacular Civilization
Examining the visual nature of Roman society and the key role of spectacular display; ranging from its center in the Roman Forum to its frontiers.

title: Experiencing Rome: A Visual Exploration of Antiquity's Greatest Empire
description:
S01 E02 — A Brief Survey of the Roman Empire
This lecture provides a chronological, thematic and geographical framework; understanding the visual components of the Roman Empire; especially how different forms of governments and their citizens affect their art, architecture and public display.

title: Experiencing Rome: A Visual Exploration of Antiquity's Greatest Empire
description:
S01 E03 — Power, Conquest, and Romanization
Learning the fundamental role of Rome's military in expanding the empire through conquest; creating and projecting the image of Roman power; introducing non-Romans to Roman values and identity.

title: Experiencing Rome: A Visual Exploration of Antiquity's Greatest Empire
description:
S01 E04 — Triumphal Processions-Victory Parades
Conquest provides a reason for triumphal processions, sacrifices, games and other grand spectacles; it also allows for public and religious participation in a reinforcement of Roman values and identity.

title: Experiencing Rome: A Visual Exploration of Antiquity's Greatest Empire
description:
S01 E05 — Imperial Palaces
Touring the palaces of Rome's powerful rulers; seeing how power and culture are displayed in forms that are admired and imitated by lower social classes.

title: Experiencing Rome: A Visual Exploration of Antiquity's Greatest Empire
description:
S01 E06 — The Roman House-Space and Decoration
As a stage for political, religious and social display, the houses of Roman elites celebrate Roman virtues and cultural identity; reinforcing to social equals and inferiors the influence of the inhabitants.

title: Great Battles of the Ancient World
description:
S01 E01 — Why Study Battles? What Is War?
Garrett G. Fagan addresses the importance of studying battles and surveys the changing scholarly approach to the subject; he concludes by looking at different definitions of warfare, particularly the operational and social-constructivist models.

title: Great Battles of the Ancient World
description:
S01 E02 — The Problem of Warfare's Origins
Three types of evidence shed light on the origins of warfare; human remains bearing evidence of trauma; artifacts that function primarily as weapons; fortifications or depictions of warriors painted on cave walls; their interpretations are tricky.

title: Great Battles of the Ancient World
description:
S01 E03 — Sumer, Akkad, and Early Mesopotamian Warfare
Written records first become available in the historical era; evidence reconstructs the conventions and conditions of warfare among the first cities in Sumer circa the 30th century B.C.; exploring the nature of Sumerian armies and battle tactics.

title: Great Battles of the Ancient World
description:
S01 E04 — Egyptian Warfare From the Old to New Kingdoms
Evidence of warfare in Ancient Egypt is ambiguous, but it is much more plentiful in later periods; the pharaoh's role is increasingly that of a war leader; Egyptian warfare is transformed by the introduction of the chariot.

title: Great Battles of the Ancient World
description:
S01 E05 — The Battles of Megiddo and Kadesh
In the New Kingdom of Egypt, one gets the first fully recorded battle in history, the Battle of Megiddo; covering the later Battle of Kadesh, which is attested in both Egyptian and Hittite accounts.
